assumptions: Plan7 Viterbi and Forward under HMMER 3.4’s reference (generic) DP, in local or glocal mode.
The E-value is the model’s own Forward statistics scaled by Z, the size of the database.
limits: Scores every sequence with the reference DP and reports every one, however poor: it runs none of hmmsearch’s acceleration filters, so a sequence the real program would drop at the MSV filter is still scored here.
A model without STATS lines has bit scores and no E-value.
bio.jane/contract.question: How well does each sequence score against this profile HMM, where does the model match, and does it clear the family’s own gathering cutoff?

description: Score sequences against ONE profile HMM on this machine, as hmmsearch scores a family against a set: per sequence a Forward and a Viterbi bit score, an E-value when the model is calibrated, every domain with its model and sequence span and its three-line alignment, and the family's own gathering-cutoff verdict when the model publishes one (Pfam does).

Z.description: the database size each E-value is scaled by. 0 takes the number of sequences screened, which is what hmmsearch does with the database it searched; set it to compare against a larger search.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

alphabet.description: what the sequences are. `auto` reads them the way HMMER does (Easel’s composition rule). Set it when a short or unusual set is read wrongly: every DNA base is also an amino-acid letter, so a nucleotide set against a protein model scores without complaint and means nothing. Values: auto (Auto (Easel’s rule)), protein (Protein), nucleotide (Nucleotide). Advanced.

include_subject.description: also screen the open or wired record (a protein record by its residues).

mode.description: `local` finds the model anywhere in a sequence, as hmmsearch does: right for a domain inside a longer protein. `glocal` makes the whole model align, which a full-length member of the family can and a fragment cannot. Values: local (Local (hmmsearch)), glocal (Glocal (whole model)).

multihit.description: allow several separate domains in one sequence (the J state). Off allows one: right when a family occurs once per protein.

pfam.description: a Pfam accession (PF and five digits): the family’s current HMM is fetched from InterPro for this run. Its gathering cutoff comes with it.

profile.description: the `.hmm` file to score against, by name, from the project or the `_files` sent with the call. Left empty with no `profile_text` or `pfam`, the one `.hmm` present is used, and several are refused by name.

profile_text.description: the model itself as HMMER3 text; wire `hmm_build`’s `hmm` here to screen with a model you just built. Advanced.

sequences.description: the sequences to screen: wire upstream records or sequences, or list library documents. A multi-record file named whole contributes every record. Gaps are removed before scoring.

name: hmm_search

hits.description: one row per sequence, best Forward score first: name, length, forwardBits, viterbiBits, forwardEvalue (absent for an uncalibrated model), membership against the gathering cutoff, and each domain’s seqFrom/seqTo (1-based) and hmmFrom/hmmTo with its alignment

members.description: sequences at or above the family’s gathering cutoff (0 when the model publishes none)

profile.description: the model screened against: name, accession, match states, alphabet, cutoffs, whether it carries E-value statistics
